description: We are the marsgency AI team! We are developing an AI-powered emergency assistant for astronauts on Mars. Our project solves multiple critical emergency scenarios using NASA data. Our team is currently full, focusing on AI development and UI design.
summary:
Marsgency
--------------------------------------------------------
NASA-Powered Terminal Emergency Intelligence AI
--------------------------------------------------------
MARSGENCY is a fully terminal-based, open-source emergency intelligence assistant. It combines a local/offline-first AI analysis layer (Gemma 4-oriented) with real NASA scientific data connectors, cached retrieval, RAG-ready reference documents, and structured emergency reporting.

Note:Terminal-only application. No GUI, no web dashboard, no browser interface, no desktop app.
details:
MARSGENCY – NASA-Powered Terminal Emergency Intelligence AI

MARSGENCY is an open-source, terminal-based emergency intelligence assistant designed to collect, analyze, and present scientific data from NASA to help users understand potential emergency situations.

The project integrates multiple NASA data sources, including NASA FIRMS, EONET, POWER, DONKI, NeoWs, and GIBS, to retrieve information about natural disasters, wildfires, extreme weather events, space weather, and near-Earth objects. It combines this information with a locally operated AI analysis system based on Google's Gemma 4 model to generate structured, evidence-based emergency assessments.

MARSGENCY works through a command-line interface rather than a graphical application, making it lightweight, accessible, and suitable for different operating systems. Its AI engine analyzes retrieved information and organizes results into situation summaries, verified data, threat assessments, recommended precautions, sources, and uncertainty reports. It also supports offline operation through locally cached NASA data and reference documents, allowing users to access previously retrieved information even without an internet connection.

The primary benefit of MARSGENCY is bringing scientific data and artificial intelligence together in a single, accessible tool. Instead of relying entirely on potentially unreliable information, the system prioritizes verifiable scientific observations, clearly identifies outdated or unavailable data, and distinguishes AI-generated risk assessments from official emergency warnings.

The project was developed using Python, with Typer and Rich for its interactive terminal interface, SQLite for local data caching, and Ollama-compatible local inference for AI capabilities. NASA's publicly available APIs provide the scientific data used by the system. The architecture is modular, allowing additional data sources, AI models, and intelligence capabilities to be integrated in the future.

What makes MARSGENCY creative is its combination of local AI, real scientific data, offline capabilities, and uncertainty-aware emergency analysis in a lightweight terminal application. Rather than simply generating answers, it aims to connect AI reasoning with actual observations and their sources.

During development, important considerations included data reliability, source transparency, privacy, offline accessibility, performance, cross-platform compatibility, and responsible AI usage. The system avoids fabricating scientific observations and explicitly communicates uncertainty and data freshness.

The intended impact of MARSGENCY is to make scientific information more accessible and useful for emergency awareness, research, and situational understanding. Ultimately, the project explores how open-source technology and locally operated AI can help people better understand risks on Earth and in space.
